sentences.text: This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sidda Ramaiah.K.O was died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 29.12.2023 at about 05.45 pm.

sentences.text:
The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
On 29.12.2023 at about 05.45pm, the deceased Sidda Ramaiah.K.O was riding a motor cycle Honda Plus bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EX-0437, on Bengaluru-Tumkur- NH-48 road, towards Tumkur along with his wife as a pillion rider to Hiriyur when they reached near Kattihole at Buddihal Gate U turn, at that time a unknown vehicle came with high sped in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against them from behind.
Due to impact, the rider and pillion rider fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
Immediately deceased was shifted to Nelamangala Government Hospital.
Later he was admitted to Victoria hospital wherein he did not succeed, he was succumbed to the injuries on 30.12.2023.
Body was shifted to Victoria Hospital and Post-Mortem was conducted and handed over the body to the petitioners.

The petitioners performed funeral and obsequious ceremonies by spending Rs.1,20,000/-.
3.
It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident deceased was hale and healthy, doing Mason Work and earning Rs.30,00/- Per month.
The deceased was maintaining the family members.
Due to the sudden and untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are terribly and mentally shocked and they have lost love and affection of the deceased.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending motor cycle Honda plus bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EX-0437 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. The accident in question was taken place due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle Honda Plus bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EX- 0437.
The The accident caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle Honda Plus bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EX-0437.
The Nelamangala Police have registered a case against the driver of the Car and filed charge sheet against him in Cr.No.056/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 304(A) of IPC.
For the aforesaid reasons, the claimants have prayed for awarding total compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- under various heads.
5. In pursuance of the notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement.

In spite of due service of notice the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed ex- parte.
5A.
The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement denying the entire petition averments.
Further denied the issuance of policy in respect of Car bearing No.KA-16-EX-0437 as on the date of alleged accident.
The rider has no having DL to drive the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
It has denied the manner of accident.
Further denied the expenses towards medical and funeral.
It has also denied the age, income, avocation of the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant.

Hence, the respondent No.
prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

14. It is to be noticed that the provisions contained under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, has been enunciated as a social security measure, by the Legislature.

As per amendment to motor vehicle Act, section 164 of Motor Vehicle Act reads thus:
"164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grevious hurt, etc.--(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section."
15.
It provides for compensation based on the structured formula method contained in Second Schedule of the said Act.
The claimants need not prove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle for claiming compensation under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It is worth to note herein that the section 163A was the enable provision prior to amendment.

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in decision reported 1(2009) 6 SCC 121, as under:
"34. . . . . . . Section 163-A of the MV 1 Sarla Verma - V/s - Delhi Transport Corporation and Another Act contains a special provision as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis, as indicated in the Second Schedule to the Act.

entities.text: MV 1 Sarla Verma - V/s - Delhi Transport Corporation and Another Act
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Second Schedule contains a table prescribing the compensation to be awarded with reference to the age and income of the deceased.
It specifies the amount of compensation to be awarded with reference to the annual income range of Rs 3,000 to Rs 40,000.
It does not specify the quantum of compensation in case the annual income of the deceased is more than Rs 40,000.
But it provides the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
The table starts with a multiplier of 15, goes up to 18, and then steadily comes down to 5.
It also provides the standard deduction as one-third on account of personal living expenses of the deceased.

Therefore, where the application is under Section 163-A of the Act, it is Vanisri vs Mallesh Naik on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81529020/
5 possible to calculate the compensation on the structured formula basis, even where the compensation is not specified with reference to the annual income of the deceased, or is more than Rs 40,000, by applying the formula: (2/3  AI  M), that is two thirds of the annual income multiplied by the multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased would be the compensation.
Several principles of tortuous liability are excluded when the claim is under Section 163-A of the MV Act."

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 2 (2013) 9 SCC 65 has held as under:
"The 1988 Act gives choice to the claimants to seek compensation on structured formula basis as provided in Section 163-A or make an application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of Section 165 under Section 166.
The claimants have to elect one of the two remedies provided in Section 163A and Section 166.
The remedy provided in Section 163-A is not a remedy in addition to the remedy provided in Section 166 but it provides for an alternative course to Section 166.

By incorporating Section 163-A in the 1988 Act, the Parliament has provided the remedy for payment of 2 Reshma Kumari & Ors -Vs- Madan Mohan & Anr compensation notwithstanding anything contained in the 1988 Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, that the owner of a motor vehicle or authorized insurer shall be liable to pay compensation on structured formula basis as indicated in the Second Schedule in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle.

entities.text: Reshma Kumari & Ors -Vs- Madan Mohan & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The peculiar feature of Section 163-A is that for a claim made there under, the claimants are not required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner or owners of the vehicle concerned.

The scheme of Section 163-A is a departure from the general principle of law of tort that the liability of the owner of the vehicle to compensate the victim or his heirs in a motor accident arises only on the proof of negligence on the part of the driver.

Section 163-A has done away with the requirement of the proof of negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle where the victim of an accident or his dependants elect to apply for compensation under Section 163- A.
When an application for compensation is made under Section 163-A the compensation is paid as indicated in the Second Schedule."

18. Our Hon'ble High Court in the case reported in 32007 SCC ONLINE KAR 538=ILR 2008 KAR 1249 has held as follows:
"MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - SECTION 163-A Petition under - Award - Accident occurred due to the negligence of the victim himself - Maintainability of petition under Section 163A - HELD, A petition under Section 163A of the act is maintainable even in case where negligence is on the part of the victim - FURTHER HELD,
Even 'Obiter Dicta' made in the decision of the Supreme Court is binding on the High Court."

Further, Our Hon'ble High Court held in a decision reported in 42008 SCC Online Kar 19=ILR 3 Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., -Vs- Smt. Salma and Others 4 National Insurance Company Limited -Vs- Honnappa and others 2008 KAR 959 as follows:
 "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 -  SECTION 163(1) - Claim petition - Maintainability of - Involvement of two motor vehicles - Accident - Injuries sustained by the claimant - Grievance of the Insurance Company - Claimant, himself being the cause for the accident,
whether can maintain the petition under Section 163-A of the Act - Award of compensation - Challenge to - HELD, When two motor vehicles were involved in the accident due to which claimant sustained injuries, in such a situation, the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Act is permissible, no matter, the driver or the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident, may 11 M.V.C.
NO. 215/2017 dispute his negligence in the matter - Hence, the tribunal has not committed any error in entertaining the petition under Section 163-A of the Act - ON FACTS, FURTHER HELD, As the entitlement of the Petitioner has been considered and awarded on structured formula basis in terms of Schedule-II of the Act, the appeal filed by the Petitioner is devoid of merits and the same is dismissed."
20.

Further, our Hon'ble High Court in the case of 5Smt. M. Malini and another -Vs - ICICI Lombard Motor Insurance and others has held as follows:
"(B) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sections 163-A and 173(1) - Appeal - Maintainability of - In instant case claimants wife and minor daughter of deceased filed claim petition for compensation under Section 163-A of the Act - Same dismissed on ground that claimants not succeeded in proving negligence on behalf of rider of the motorcycle - Appellants/claimants filed an Appeal against impugned order dismissing claim petition- Allowed on the ground that claimants/Appellants were not under obligation to prove negligency committed by the driver of the offending vehicle where claim petition for compensation filed under Section 163-A of the Act- Hence appeal against impugned order maintainable."
21.

Further, our Hon'ble High Court in the 5 2016 Kant M.A.C. 105 (Kant) case of United India Insurance Company Limited - V/s - Smt. Rajamma and Others (M.F.A. No. 10292/2012 dated 11-11-2016) has categorically held in paragraph 14 of the said Order that when two motor vehicles are involved in the accident, irrespective of the negligence or default of the owner/driver of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person, claim under Section 163-A is maintainable.

sentences.text: In the said decision, our Hon'ble High Court has been pleased to follow the earlier Division Bench judgment in Appaji's case (2004 ACJ 1289) to hold that non-impleadment of the owner or driver of the vehicle involved in the accident is not fatal to claim compensation under Section 163-A of the Act.

22. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held in a decision reported (2019) 12 SCC 398 has held "the grant of compensation under section 163-A on the basis of the structured formula is in the Vanisri vs Mallesh Naik on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81529020/
7 nature of a final award and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle(s) 6 United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Sunil Kumar and another involved in the accident- Further,
though section 163-A does not specifically exclude a possible defense of the insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated by section 140(4), to permit such defense to be introduced by the insurer and/or to understand the provision of Sec.163-A to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163-A,
namely final compensation within a limited time-frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situations where the claims of the compensation on the basis of fault liability were taking an unduly long time-

Further, to understand section 163-A to permit the insurer to raise the defense of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under section 163-A on a par with proceedings under section 166 which would not only be self contradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention-Thus, in a proceeding under section 163-A of the Act, it is not open for the insurer to raise any defense of negligence on the part of the victim"
23.

Thus, in view of the above principles, I am of the humble opinion that this Court cannot go into the question of determining the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, when the petition is filed under Section 163-A or 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

24. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in the case of Pratima W/o Madivalappa Naikar and others Vs Thalkin Ahamad B.A and others7 held in paragraph No.20 that:
"20.

Relying on this judgment we are of the considered view that the appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.5 lakshs."
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation Rs.5,00,000/-.
Hence, it is appears to Court that the petitioners have proved their case by adducing cogent evidence.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 and 2 in the affirmative and issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation from the respondent No.1.
